NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, APRIL
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D

CASE AGAINST YOUNG BRITON

Opening of Proceedings Against Warren Martin
in H. M. Police Court

After a week's adjournment due to the prosecution's inability to produce its witnesses, the case of Rex. v. Warren M. Martin, twenty-one year old Briton, came up before Mr. I. T. Morris, acting Registrar, in H. M. Police Court yesterday, and after a number of witnesses for the prosecution had been heard, was adjourned for a week.

The case is a sequel to an accident on the Shanghai-Hangchow highway last year when a car which the accused was driving killed a Chinese woman. Mr. John McNeill is appearing for the prosecution under instructions from the Crown Advocate, while the accused is represented by Mr. H. Lipson-Ward.

"This prosecution," said Mr. McNeill, opening the case, "concerns an occurrence which took place in December last year on the Shanghai-Hangchow highway, between Kangpu and Changchuan. A plan of the scene will be produced, which shows that an accident took place at or on a bridge which just past a fairly right-angled bend in the road.

"Evidence will be produced as to the nature of the road and the materials with which the bridge was built. A number of Chinese were present, one of whom was killed

The Sound of an Engine

"The evidence will go to show that they were walking along the road when they heard the engine of an approaching car. They went to the south side of the bridge (the left side as you approach it). One of them, a woman, saw the car, which swerved to the right and then turned and dashed at them. The woman who was killed was struck in the stomach and crushed against the wooden parapet of the bridge. Evidence will also be produced as to the braking capacity of this particular car."

Pan Ting-ping, first departmental chief of the Haiyen Bureau of Public Safety, entered the witness-box, and said that 12.30 p.m. on December 5 last year he and his second, as a result of a telephone call from the 2nd Police Sub-Station, went to the Haiyen bus station, where he found Martin, Mr. Victor Stott, and their car.

They drove to the scene of the accident in the car; when he arrived at the bridge he saw the woman's body. After placing a man on guard, he examined the scene. On approaching the bridge from the east, a sharp curve was encountered. This was sign-posted by a board placed 90 metres from the curve. The weather that day was fine, and the road was dry.

Cross-examined by Mr. Lipson-Ward:—Accident took place on December 5, 1933, summons was issued on March 23, 1934. He could not explain the delay. He denied that when he met the accused and Stott that they said they had come to report the accident to the police, or that they mentioned a little child as having run across in front of the car—they did mention that she had been injured, however.

Car Detained

In response to further questions, he said that after examining the scene, he returned to Haiyen with Martin and Stott, the husband of the dead woman following later. They took the girl with them to a hospital, where she was treated.

The two young men gave him their names and addresses, and on arrival at the police-station, their passports were examined. The passports showed them to be British.

Mr. Lipson-Ward:—Didn't you tell them they could not leave the police-station?—We had to detain their car as we had orders to do so in cases of accidents. They could leave.

Do you tell the magistrate that you did not tell them to remain in the station?

Mr. McNeill:—I don't see where this is leading to.

Mr. Lipson-Ward:—You will, if you wait.

Mr. McNeill:—I hope it is relevant.

Mr. Lipson-Ward:—I don't ask irrelevant questions.

The witness here denied that they were not allowed to leave. They were told they could write if they wanted to, but they could not phone, as there were no through-wires. There never was any suggestion that they were not free to leave.

Request for Compensation

At 3 o'clock the next afternoon, went on the witness in reply to questions, the dead woman's husband came and asked for $1,000 for compensation.

Didn't you and the other police tell these gentlemen that they could go when they paid up?—We did not say they could not leave, they could go when the matter was completed.

"A distinction without a difference" Commented Mr. Lipson-Ward.

Three days after the accident, Mr. Martin, senior, Mr. R. Cooke, and a Mr. Yang from the Shanghai Bureau of Public Safety arrived, and they all went to the magistrate's office in Haiyen. The deceased's husband was also present. He recollected telling them throughout that there was no charge against them, and that the matter would be satisfactorily closed on payment to deceased's husband of $650. He identified a receipt signed at this transaction.

They all then left, but returned two or three days later, when he entertained them to tiffin in the police-station. He never suggested to them that they had committed a criminal offence.

The Accident Described

The next witness, Chu Wu-sze, said she was from the village of Sheng-weili. She was one of the party and saw the accident. They were all returning home at the time, after buying a quantity of potatoes at the Changchuan Bar. They heard a car coming, they crossed the bridge, all except the little girl, and they all went to the left-hand side. She described how it swerved to the right, and then towards them, hitting Wong Ong-sze, the deceased, and her daughter. It then immediately returned to the east, where it was coming from.

Cross-examined, she denied hearing a horn blow or that the young girl ran across in front of the car. They were all leaning on the wooden parapet of the bridge as the car approached.

Other witnesses called were Pan Tse-sah, who gave his profession as an "examiner of dead bodies in the district of Chekiang Province," and who described the injuries received by the deceased, and other members of the party, including Wong Yu-pao, of whom gave corroborative evidence.

Little Yu-pao, fifteen years old, looked rather scared as she entered the witness-box, and could not gather the meaning of the oath. She promised, however, to tell the truth. She corroborated Chu Wu-sze's story, and said she had been struck on the front of her right knee.

Concern over Potatoes

Two witness of the same name, Tsu Lee-sze, both women, were called, and gave similar evidence. The second of the two, however, said in cross-examination that she did not notice the car return, or see any police. The whole party left soon after, leaving Yu-pao crying beside her dead mother's body. No one looked after her.

"So what it comes to," said Mr. Lipson-Ward," is that you left the girl and the dead woman, and went off with your potatoes?"

Through the interpreter, witness said that they were in a hurry to go home.

After the first witness had been recalled to give evidence as to why one of the party of witnesses could not be called—he had not been located—the acting Registrar adjourned the case to 10 a.m. on Tuesday, April 24.

针对一名英国青年的案件

在华洋巡捕房对沃伦·马丁提起诉讼的开庭审理

由于控方无法传唤其证人出庭，案件休庭一周后，雷克斯诉沃伦·M·马丁案（被告为一名二十一岁的英国人）昨日由代理推事 I. T. 莫里斯在华洋巡捕房开庭审理。在听取数名控方证人的证词后，案件再次休庭一周。

本案是去年发生在沪杭公路上的一起事故的后续，当时被告驾驶的汽车撞死了一名中国妇女。约翰·麦克尼尔先生奉皇家检察官之命代表控方出庭，而被告则由 H. 利普森-沃德先生代表。

麦克尼尔先生在开场陈述中说：“本次起诉涉及去年十二月发生在沪杭公路上、康浦与长川之间的一起事件。我们将提交一份现场平面图，显示事故发生在或靠近一座桥梁处，该桥位于道路一个近乎直角的弯道之后。

“我们将提供关于道路性质及建桥材料的证据。当时有多名中国人在场，其中一人遇难。

引擎声

“证据将表明，他们正沿路行走时，听到一辆 approaching 汽车的引擎声。他们走到桥的南侧（即接近桥时的左侧）。其中一名妇女看到了那辆汽车，该车先向右急转，随后掉头向他们冲来。遇难的妇女腹部受到撞击，并被挤压在桥的木质护栏上。我们还将提供关于这辆特定汽车制动能力的证据。”

海盐县公安局第一科科长潘廷平进入证人席作证称，去年12月5日下午12时30分，他接到第二警察分局的电话后，与其副手前往海盐汽车站，在那里发现了马丁、维克多·斯托特先生及其汽车。

他们驾车前往事故现场；当他到达桥头时，看到了那名妇女的尸体。他在安排一人看守现场后，对现场进行了勘查。从东面接近桥梁时，会遇到一个急弯。在距离弯道90米处设有一块标示牌。当天天气晴朗，路面干燥。

经利普森-沃德先生盘问：— 事故发生在1933年12月5日，传票于1934年3月23日发出。他无法解释这一延误。他否认在与被告和斯托特会面时，对方曾表示他们是来向警方报告事故的，或者提到有一个小孩跑到车前——不过他们确实提到了有人受伤。

扣留汽车

在回答进一步提问时，他说，在勘查现场后，他与马丁和斯托特返回海盐，死者丈夫随后也到了。他们将那名女孩带到医院接受治疗。

这两名年轻人向他提供了姓名和地址，到达警察局后，查验了他们的护照。护照显示他们是英国人。

利普森-沃德先生：— 您没有告诉他们不能离开警察局吗？— 我们必须扣留他们的汽车，因为我们有命令要求在发生事故时这样做。他们可以离开。

您是否告诉推事，您没有要求他们留在警局？

麦克尼尔先生：— 我看不出这有什么关联。

利普森-沃德先生：— 如果您等着，就会明白。

麦克尼尔先生：— 我希望这与案件有关。

利普森-沃德先生：— 我不问无关的问题。

证人此时否认他们不被允许离开。他们被告知如果想写信可以写，但不能打电话，因为没有直通线路。从未有过暗示说他们不自由离开。

赔偿要求

证人在回答提问时继续说道，次日下午3点，死者丈夫前来要求赔偿1,000美元。

您和其他警察没有告诉这些绅士，只要付钱就可以走吗？— 我们没有说他们不能离开，事情处理完后他们就可以走。

“毫无区别的区分”，利普森-沃德先生评论道。

事故发生三天后，老马丁先生、R. 库克先生以及来自上海市公安局的一位杨先生抵达，他们都去了海盐的 magistrate's office（推事办公室/县公署）。死者丈夫也在场。他记得一直告诉他们，对他们没有任何指控，只要向死者丈夫支付650美元，此事即可满意地结案。他指认了在此交易中签署的一张收据。

随后他们都离开了，但两三天后又回来了，他在警察局请他们吃了便饭。他从未向他们暗示过他们犯了刑事罪。

事故描述

下一位证人朱五氏（音译）说，她来自盛围里村。她是同行者之一，目睹了事故。当时她们在长川坝买了许多土豆后正回家。她们听到一辆汽车驶来，除了那个小女孩外，大家都过了桥，都走到了左侧。她描述了汽车如何先向右急转，然后朝她们冲来，撞到了死者黄翁氏（音译）和她的女儿。随后汽车立即返回其来的东方。

经盘问，她否认听到鸣笛声，也否认看到小女孩跑到车前。当汽车接近时，她们都靠在桥的木质护栏上。

其他被传唤的证人包括潘泽萨（音译），其职业自称为“浙江省验尸员”，他描述了死者所受的伤害；以及同行的其他成员，包括黄玉宝（音译），他们提供了佐证。

十五岁的小玉宝（音译）进入证人席时看起来相当害怕，无法理解宣誓的含义。但她承诺会说真话。她证实了朱五氏的说法，并说她的右膝前部受到了撞击。

对土豆的关注

两名同名女性证人祖李氏（音译）被传唤，提供了类似的证词。然而，第二位证人在盘问中表示，她没有注意到汽车返回，也没有看到任何警察。整个团体不久后离开，留下玉宝在她死去母亲的尸体旁哭泣。无人照顾她。

“所以归根结底，”利普森-沃德先生说，“你们丢下女孩和死者，带着你们的土豆走了？”

通过翻译，证人说她们急着回家。

在第一位证人被重新传唤以解释为何一名同行证人未能出庭——因为未找到此人——之后，代理推事将案件休庭至4月24日星期二上午10点。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, APRIL 11, 1934

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. D. REGISTRY.
No. D 5529
Date 12 / 1 / 34

MANSLAUGHTER CASE
BEFORE COURT

Sequel To An Accident On
Hangchow Highway;
Briton Charged

A sequel to the motor car accident which occurred on the Hangchow Highway, on December 5 last year, was heard in the British Police Court yesterday when Warren M. Martin, young Briton, was charged before Acting Registrar I. T. Morris with having unlawfully killed one, Wong Ongsze, a Chinese woman. The defendant was represented by Mr. H. Lipson Ward. Mr. John McNeill conducted the prosecution.

Mr. McNeill applied for an adjournment of the hearing for two weeks on the ground that his witnesses were not present in court.

This was strenuously opposed by Mr. Ward, who pointed out the gravity of the charge against the defendant. He stated that the summons had been applied for and served on March 23 and the prosecution had had ample time in which to have their witnesses ready.

The Court adjourned the hearing until April 17.

It will be recalled that on April 5, two young Britons, Warren Martin and Victor G. Stott, while motoring on the Hangchow Highway, were involved in a motor accident in which a Chinese woman was knocked down and injured. The two foreigners were immediately seized by Chinese police in the vicinity and detained at the police station at Haiyen. They managed to have a message conveyed to their parents in Shanghai and, accompanied by a police officer from the Shanghai Municipal Police, a party proceeded to Haiyen. It is understood that the matter was then satisfactorily settled by the payment of compensation to the injured woman, and the two foreigners were released and returned to Shanghai.

The injured woman subsequently died, with the result that a charge of unlawful killing has been brought against Warren Martin, who is alleged to have been driving the car at the time of the accident.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事与搜查登记处。
编号 D 5529
日期 34年1月12日

过失杀人案
法庭审理

沪杭公路事故后续；
英国人被控

去年12月5日发生在沪杭公路上的汽车事故有了后续，昨日在华洋巡捕房进行了审理，英国青年沃伦·M·马丁被控非法杀害一名中国妇女黄翁氏（音译）。被告由 H. 利普森·沃德先生代表。约翰·麦克尼尔先生负责公诉。

麦克尼尔先生以证人未出庭为由，申请将听证会延期两周。

此举遭到沃德先生的强烈反对，他指出针对被告的指控性质严重。他指出，传票已于3月23日申请并送达，控方有充足的时间准备证人。

法庭将听证会延期至4月17日。

回顾一下，4月5日，两名英国青年沃伦·马丁和维克多·G·斯托特在沪杭公路驾车时卷入一起车祸，一名中国妇女被撞倒受伤。这两名外国人随即被附近的中国警察抓获，并拘留在海盐警察局。他们设法将消息传递给在上海的父母，随后，在一位上海公共租界工部局警务处警官的陪同下，一行人前往海盐。据悉，当时通过向受伤妇女支付赔偿金，此事已得到满意解决，两名外国人获释并返回上海。

受伤妇女随后死亡，导致对沃伦·马丁提出非法杀人的指控，据称事故发生时由他驾驶汽车。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, DECEMBER 9, 1933 S. B. R C
British Motorists Return
To Shanghai Home
No. D_______
H.B.M. Consular Authorities To Send To Nanking
Message Of Appreciation Of Treatment Of
Young Men By Haiyen Officials

Released after private negotiation, Warren Martin (20) and Victor G. Stott (23), the two Britons who had been detained at Haiyen (Chekiang)—more for their own protection than anything else—since Tuesday following an accident in which a Chinese woman and child were injured by their car, returned to Shanghai early yesterday morning, none the worse for their experience. They stated that they were extremely well treated by the Haiyen authorities and that their detention was due solely to the attitude of the villagers and farmers.

The British Consulate-General is conveying to the Nanking Government its appreciation of the treatment these two young men received from the Haiyen officials.

Martin and Stott, employed respectively by Mutual Advertisers and the Burroughs-Wellcome Company, left Shanghai by motor car last Tuesday morning for Hangchow, to spend about a week holiday-making in that locality. The first intimation that anything untoward had occurred came on Wednesday evening, when Mr. F. E. Martin, of 610 Rue Lafayette and Dodwell and Company, Ltd., received a letter on a scrap of paper from Stott, describing what had happened and asking that some money should be brought down.

Paying Expenses:
After informing the British Consulate-General of the incident, Mr. Martin set out from Shanghai by car on Thursday morning with a companion and an officer of the Public Safety Bureau. Arriving at Haiyen in the afternoon, Mr. Martin negotiated with officials there, and on his agreeing to pay a small sum that is understood to represent the expenses incurred by the woman and child as a result of the mishap the villagers were satisfied and the two young men released. That night the party set out in the two cars for Shanghai, arriving here about 2.30 a.m. yesterday.

From the account of their experiences given by Martin and Stott it appears that they made good time from Shanghai towards Hangchow on Tuesday. They had tiffin on the road and had reached Haiyen, which is on the highway not far past Chapoo, about 2 p.m. As they approached a bridge on the outskirts of that town they saw seated on one side of it about half a dozen women. On the other was a little girl.

As the travellers approached they sounded the horn. One of the women, apparently the mother of the child, at once called to it, and the child rose and started to walk across the bridge right in front of the car. The driver jambed on the brakes and the car, skidding in the loose gravel, became out of control. It struck one of the women, injuring her about the body, and inflicted slight cuts on the child.

Anxious Moments
Then occurred what was apparently the only ugly incident in the whole affair. Within a few minutes a crowd of some hundreds of angry farmers and villagers had gathered threateningly around the car and the motorists had some anxious moments before the local police intervened, and gave them protection.

Owing to the temper of the crowd, which was in no mood to be gainsaid, it is understood, the magistrate of Haiyer impounded the car and placed the two travellers under detention. They were not locked up in a cell but were kept at the police station, which is a quite substantial building.

Both the magistrate and his wife, Martin and Stott said, treated them with the greatest consideration. The wife procured from somewhere a foreign bed for them and by the morning had by some unknown means obtained for them Shanghai-made bread and foreign butter, together with other foreign food. They were able also to post the express letter that brought Mr. Martin to the scene.

Throughout the practically three days of their stay, the young men state, the magistrate and his wife did all that could be done for their comfort, treating them more as guests than anything else, and the parting on Thursday night left friendliness on all sides.

Consular Action
On their return the two reported to the British Consulate what had happened and the Consular authorities took immediate steps to express to the Nanking Government their appreciation of the treatment accorded the two young men by the Haiyen officials.

The experience of these two Britons shows that while motorists who are, through fault or misfortune, involved in a mishap while travelling on Chinese highways may be open to some trouble from villagers, they will receive most considerate treatment from Chinese officials.

（批：Sec. C. i）

《字林西报》，1933年12月9日，星期六 S. B. R C

英国驾车者返回上海寓所
编号 D_______
英王陛下领事当局将向南京发送讯息，感谢海盐官员对两名青年的待遇

沃伦·马丁（Warren Martin，20岁）和维克多·G·斯托特（Victor G. Stott，23岁），这两名英国人自上周二以来一直被拘留在海盐（浙江）——这更多是为了保护他们自身安全，而非其他原因——起因是他们的汽车撞伤了一名中国妇女和一名儿童。经过私下谈判后，他们于昨日清晨返回上海，未因这段经历受到任何伤害。他们表示，海盐当局对他们待遇极佳，其被拘留完全是由于村民和农民的态度所致。

英国总领事馆正向南京政府传达其对这两名青年所受海盐官员待遇的感激之情。

马丁和斯托特分别受雇于 Mutual Advertisers 公司和 Burroughs-Wellcome 公司，于上周二上午驾车离开上海前往杭州，计划在该地度假约一周。首次得知发生不幸事件是在周三晚上，当时住在拉斐特路（Rue Lafayette）610号、任职于 Dodwell and Company, Ltd. 的 F. E. 马丁先生收到斯托特写在一张碎纸片上的信，信中描述了事发经过，并要求送些钱去。

支付费用：
在向英国总领事馆通报此事后，马丁先生于周四上午与一名同伴及一名公共租界工部局警务处（Public Safety Bureau）警官驾车从上海出发。下午抵达海盐后，马丁先生与当地官员进行谈判，在他同意支付一笔小额款项（据信该款项代表那名妇女和儿童因事故产生的费用）后，村民感到满意，两名青年获释。当晚，一行人分乘两辆汽车启程返回上海，于昨日凌晨约2点30分抵达此处。

根据马丁和斯托特对其经历的叙述，他们在周二从上海前往杭州的途中进展顺利。他们在路上用了午餐，并于下午2点左右抵达海盐，该地位于乍浦（Chapoo）不远处的公路上。当他们接近该镇郊外的一座桥梁时，看到桥的一侧坐着大约半打妇女，另一侧有一个小女孩。

当驾车者靠近时，他们按响了喇叭。其中一名妇女（显然是孩子的母亲）立即呼唤孩子，孩子站起身来，开始直接在车前横穿桥梁。司机猛踩刹车，汽车在松散的碎石路上打滑失控。汽车撞到其中一名妇女，致其身体受伤，并造成儿童轻微割伤。

焦虑时刻
随后发生了显然是整个事件中唯一不愉快的插曲。几分钟内，数百名愤怒的农民和村民聚集在车周围，气势汹汹，在当地警察介入并提供保护之前，驾车者经历了一段焦虑的时刻。

据悉，由于人群情绪激动，不容辩驳，海盐知事扣押了汽车，并将两名旅行者拘留。他们并未被关进牢房，而是被留在警察局，那是一座相当坚固的建筑。

马丁和斯托特表示，知事及其夫人对他们照顾有加。知事夫人不知从何处为他们弄来了一张西式床，并在次日早晨通过某种不明途径为他们搞到了上海制造的面包和外国黄油以及其他外国食品。他们还得以寄出那封促使马丁先生赶赴现场的加急信件。

两名青年称，在几乎三天的停留期间，知事及其夫人为他们的舒适竭尽所能，待他们更像客人而非囚犯，周四晚间的离别充满了友好气氛。

领事行动
返回后，两人向英国领事馆汇报了事发经过，领事当局立即采取措施，向南京政府表达对海盐官员给予这两名青年待遇的感激之情。

这两名英国人的经历表明，虽然驾车者在中国公路上行驶时，若因过错或不幸卷入事故，可能会遭到村民的一些麻烦，但他们将从中国官员那里得到极为周到的待遇。

（批注：Sec. C. i）
（批注：警司：请 Hunkin 阅后归还）
（批注：1933年12月15日）
SL，
请阅
并转交 W. Lay。
White.
（签名）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 8, 1933

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D
Date ___/___/___

Two Britons
Detained In
N. Chekiang

Shanghai Motorists Are
Held In Gaol When
Car Hits Woman

CHINESE DEMAND FOR
COMPENSATION

Action By H.B.M. Consulate;
Incident Not First Of
Kind On Highways

A letter on a scrap of paper has brought word to Shanghai that two young Britons from this city—Warren Martin (20) and Victor G. Stott (23)—are being detained by Chinese police at Haiyen, 29 miles from Hangchow, on the highway to Shanghai, pending payment of compensation by them for injuries received by a Chinese woman who was knocked down by their car. Martin's father left Shanghai for Haiyen yesterday to try to free the youths, and appropriate action is being taken by the British Consulate-General.

Martin, whose parents are Mr. and Mrs. F. E. Martin, of 610 Rue Lafayette, and who is employed by Mutual Advertisers, and his companion Stott, who works with Burroughs-Wellcome Company, left Shanghai at 10 a.m. last Tuesday in a Singer sports car for Hangchow, to spend about a week holiday-making in that locality. When passing through Haiyen, their car struck and injured a Chinese woman. The local police at once seized the car and placed the two youths in gaol, it is believed, to hold them until they pay compensation.

First news that anything was amiss was received late yesterday when a telegram from Stott written on a dirty scrap of paper was received by Martin's father and a similar letter by an associate at Burroughs-Wellcome. "Bring Plenty Of Money"

This letter explained how the young men came to be in gaol and their car to be impounded, said "bring plenty of money" and concluded with "For God's sake hurry." The letter said also that the Haiyen magistrate was favourably inclined towards them and that they were being well treated.

Naturally this news came as a most unpleasant shock to Martin's parents. Realizing, however, that the martial law declared in Chinese territory owing to the Fukien revolt made night travel outside the Settlement inadvisable, they made no move until yesterday morning, when the matter was reported at the British Consulate-General.

While appropriate measures were taken by Consular officials, Mr. Martin, who is manager of the machinery department of Dodwell and Company, Ltd., left Shanghai about 11 a.m. yesterday by car with a companion for Haiyen. He took with him $300 and his plan was to negotiate for the release of the two young men. If he is not successful, he will report again to the British Consulate in Shanghai, which will then, it is understood, take further action.

Late last night, Mr. Martin had neither returned to Shanghai nor communicated with his home. In view of the martial law restrictions, it is possible that whether his mission to Haiyen was successful or not, he would continue to Hangchow to stay the night there. He is expected back in Shanghai this morning.

Although naturally very upset, Mrs. Martin last night did not believe the youths to be in serious danger, regarding the action of the Haiyen police as aimed solely at obtaining compensation money. She stated that the Bureau of Public Safety sent a telegram yesterday morning to Haiyen ordering the "immediate release of the two Britishers."

This incident is by no means the only one of its kind on Chinese highways recently. Only last weekend, a well-known woman from Shanghai had her car and chauffeur detained following a similar mishap on the Hangchow highway, and was saved from extreme inconvenience herself, it is reported, only by the assistance of other motorists.

（批：D/B/C 8/12）
（批：$I, Please note and pass W.Hay. Wple. M）
（批：HR）

《字林西报》，1933年12月8日，星期五

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事侦缉处登记簿。
编号 D
日期 ___/___/___

两名英国人
在浙北
被拘留

上海驾车者
因汽车撞伤妇女
被关入监狱

中国人要求
赔偿

英王陛下领事馆采取行动；
此类事件在公路上
并非首例

一封写在碎纸片上的信给上海带来消息，称本市两名年轻英国人——沃伦·马丁（20岁）和维克多·G·斯托特（23岁）——正被中国警察拘留在海盐，该地位于杭州至上海公路上，距杭州29英里，等待他们支付赔偿金，以补偿被其汽车撞伤的一名中国妇女。马丁的父亲昨日离开上海前往海盐，试图解救这两名青年，英国总领事馆正在采取适当行动。

马丁的父母是住在拉斐特路610号的 F. E. 马丁夫妇，他受雇于 Mutual Advertisers 公司；他的同伴斯托特则在 Burroughs-Wellcome 公司工作。两人于上周二上午10点驾驶一辆辛格（Singer）跑车离开上海前往杭州，计划在该地度假约一周。途经海盐时，他们的汽车撞伤了一名中国妇女。当地警察立即扣押了汽车，并将这两名青年关入监狱，据信此举是为了扣留他们直至支付赔偿。

首次得知情况不妙是在昨天深夜，当时马丁的父亲收到了斯托特写在一张脏纸片上的电报，Burroughs-Wellcome 公司的一名同事也收到了一封类似的信件。“带足钱”

这封信解释了两名青年为何入狱以及汽车为何被扣押，信中称“带足钱”，并以“看在上帝份上，速来”结尾。信中还提到，海盐知事对他们持好感，且他们受到了良好待遇。

当然，这一消息给马丁的父母带来了极其不快的震惊。然而，考虑到因福建事变（Fukien revolt）在中国领土宣布戒严，夜间离开租界旅行并不明智，他们直到昨天早上才采取行动，当时此事已向英国总领事馆报告。

在领事官员采取适当措施的同时，任职于 Dodwell and Company, Ltd. 机械部经理的马丁先生于昨天上午11点左右与一名同伴驾车离开上海前往海盐。他随身携带了300美元，计划谈判以释放这两名青年。如果他不成功，他将再次向上海的英国领事馆报告，届时据信领事馆将采取进一步行动。

昨晚深夜，马丁先生既未返回上海，也未与家人联系。鉴于戒严限制，无论他赴海盐的任务是否成功，他都有可能继续前往杭州并在那里过夜。预计他将于今晨返回上海。

尽管自然非常不安，马丁夫人昨晚并不认为这两名青年处于严重危险之中，她认为海盐警方的行动纯粹旨在获取赔偿金。她表示，公共租界工部局警务处（Bureau of Public Safety）已于昨天上午向海盐发出电报，命令“立即释放两名英国人”。

近期在中国公路上发生的此类事件绝非仅此一例。就在上周末，一位来自上海的知名女士在杭州公路上发生类似事故后，其汽车和司机被扣留，据报道，她本人仅在其它驾车者的帮助下才免于极大的不便。
